areas.title: Imports and visibility
areas.uncovered: Filtered imports, imported membership enumeration, alias collisions through imports, and all contextual name-resolution rules remain unqualified.

areas.title: Typing
areas.uncovered: Multiple and implicit typing, chained types and all type-kind constraints need further cases.

areas.title: Specialization and inheritance
areas.uncovered: Diamond coverage is limited to a common ancestor; conflicts, cycles and all inherited memberships require broader qualification.

areas.title: Subsetting
areas.uncovered: These cases check target identity, not instance-value containment or every conformance constraint.

areas.title: Redefinition
areas.uncovered: Direction, multiplicity, featuring-type conformance and nested redefinitions need additional cases.

areas.title: Multiplicity
areas.uncovered: Only literal declared bounds are asserted; expression bounds, effective defaults and containment are unqualified.

areas.title: Conjugated port typing
areas.uncovered: These assertions cover written references, not conjugated direction/flow semantics.

areas.title: Connections and chains
areas.uncovered: Endpoint identity and arity are covered; direction, flow compatibility and connection end conformance need further cases.

areas.title: Names and source fidelity
areas.uncovered: Byte/UTF-16 mapping and recovery are project API guarantees; lexical names are the standards link. No editable CST contract is claimed.

areas.title: Cyclic input handling
areas.uncovered: Termination is an operational guarantee, not a semantic verdict about every cycle. Continuous fuzzing remains separate work.

areas.title: Lexical names and dialect boundaries
areas.uncovered: These cases exercise reserved, quoted and escaped names; all terminals, escape forms and grammar alternatives remain unqualified.

An owned name wins over an imported name.
Conflicting wildcard imports produce ambiguity.
Pinned official alias-import example resolves its original definition.
Pinned official import-all example reaches the privately imported definition.
A SysML usage resolves a KerML classifier across files.
An absent type remains unresolved.
A part typed by an attribute definition receives a semantic diagnostic.
A standard-library scalar type resolves to a library declaration.
Diamond inheritance contributes the common member once.
An absent general type is reported without inventing a target.
Missing heritage stays incomplete through definitions and typed usages.
A usage subsets the intended feature.
A missing subsetted feature remains unresolved.
A redefining feature replaces its inherited predecessor.
A missing redefinition target remains unresolved.
Literal bounds survive normalization, including an unbounded upper limit.
A reversed literal interval receives a semantic diagnostic.
Conjugated spelling is preserved while its name target resolves.
An absent conjugated port type is not silently resolved.
Binary endpoints retain their usage and port chain.
A broken final endpoint never becomes a resolved prefix.
Three written connection ends remain three semantic endpoints.
Quoted Unicode names retain exact CRLF source coordinates.
Syntax recovery retains an earlier valid declaration.
Cyclic imports terminate and preserve a reachable public definition.
Mutual specialization terminates and preserves both declarations.
Enumerate owned membership identity, alias names and short names separately from target ownership.
Resolve local, enclosing and explicitly global names with lexical shadowing.
Protected members are inherited but not externally visible; private members are not inherited.
Recursive import reaches nested public members and excludes private members.
Forward aliases resolve transitively to the original element.
Unresolved alias remains a binding with an explicit unresolved target.
Inherited memberships retain protected aliases of a nested definition and its declaring namespace; private aliases do not inherit.
Detect an owned alias colliding with an inherited member of a conforming metaclass.
Same names on unrelated metaclasses and anonymous members are distinguishable.
A short name colliding with a long name of the same metaclass is rejected.
A root namespace import must have private visibility.
A private root import is valid and visible to its nested package.
Evaluate multiplicity feature references backed by integer formulas, retaining exact bounds and unbounded/zero distinctions.
An unvalued multiplicity provider yields unknown, not a default or an empty domain.
Preserve integers beyond IEEE-754 exact range through the wire and display contracts.
Subset multiplicities inherit an interval and preserve an explicit narrower interval.
Fractional and reversed cardinality bounds are invalid and never evaluated results.
Unresolved subset targets prevent a default cardinality result.
Syntax recovery cannot erase a malformed bound and claim an implicit singleton.
Expose complete imported membership closure with completeness guarantees.
cases.planned: Owned and inherited bindings are public; complete imported membership enumeration is not yet exposed.

cases.purpose: Distinct inherited memberships of the same Feature are removed by Type::removeRedefinedFeatures; non-Feature aliases use IMP-014.
Quoted names preserve spaces, escaped quotes, Unicode and reserved words through resolution.
Unquoted SysML reserved words are rejected as identifiers and later declarations recover.
A SysML-only keyword remains a legal unquoted KerML identifier.
Aliases with equal names and unrelated target metaclasses remain distinguishable.
Alias short-name/long-name collisions of conforming target metaclasses are diagnosed.
A literal-valued scalar feature supplies exact multiplicity bounds.
Static package attribute providers retain alias identity, transitive values, range endpoints, zero, and exact large integers.
Cyclic, unvalued, variation and context-dependent providers cannot supply checked static bounds.
Evaluate arithmetic-valued package providers with complete canonical argument bindings, retaining exact integer results.
Undefined, non-natural, out-of-range, cyclic and unbound arithmetic providers cannot supply checked numeric bounds.
A user package shadowing DataFunctions cannot be used to certify a designated arithmetic operator.
A valid conditional-valued provider should select the true branch for a static multiplicity bound.

knownFailures.reason: The canonical graph preserves conditional operand wrappers, but the checked expression provider does not yet certify conditional invocation and branch selection. Retain the expected exact result.
